turns.prompt_text: I have a Chevy Malibu and I'd like to put a hitch on it. How can I go about doing that?
turns.response_html:
Installing a hitch on a Chevy Malibu is a very common DIY project, especially if you’re looking to use a hitch-mounted bike rack or a small cargo tray. Since the Malibu is a unibody sedan, you’ll be installing a Receiver Hitch (usually Class 1 or 2) that bolts directly to the vehicle's frame.

Here is the step-by-step process to get it done:

1. Choose the Right Hitch

You need a hitch specifically engineered for your Malibu's model year. Most Malibus use a 1.25-inch receiver (Class 1 or 2).

  • Weight Rating: These are typically rated for a 2,000 lb. towing capacity and a 200 lb. tongue weight.
  • Brands: Look for reputable brands like Curt or Draw-Tite. They provide vehicle-specific instructions and custom-fit hardware.

2. Gather Your Tools

Most modern hitch installs for this car are "bolt-on," meaning no welding is required, though you may need to do some minor "fishing" of bolts through the frame.

  • Socket set (usually 11/16", 3/4", or metric equivalents)
  • Torque wrench (essential for safety)
  • Jack and jack stands (to give yourself more working room)
  • A "fish wire" or "pull wire" (usually included with the hitch kit)

3. The Installation Process

While specific steps vary by year, the general workflow for a Malibu is:

  • Lower the Exhaust: You will likely need to temporarily pop a couple of rubber exhaust hangers off to let the muffler drop a few inches. This gives you room to reach the frame rails.
  • Fish the Bolts: You’ll use the provided pull-wires to feed carriage bolts and square-hole spacers through access holes in the frame and down through the mounting holes.
  • Position the Hitch: This is much easier with a second person. Lift the hitch into place, aligning the holes with the bolts you just fished through.
  • Secure the Hardware: Hand-tighten the nuts onto the bolts. Once everything is aligned, use your torque wrench to tighten them to the manufacturer’s specific foot-pound rating.
  • Reattach Exhaust: Lift the muffler back into place and slide the rubber hangers back on.

4. Considerations for Your Malibu

  • Ground Clearance: The Malibu sits relatively low. Keep in mind that a hitch will reduce your departure angle, so be careful going over steep driveways or speed bumps.
  • Wiring: If you plan on actually towing a small trailer (rather than just using a bike rack), you’ll need to install a T-One or similar wiring harness to power the trailer lights. These usually plug directly into your existing tail light factory harness.

Pro Tip: If you aren't comfortable working under the car or "fishing" bolts into the frame, many U-Haul locations or local independent shops can perform the install for a flat labor fee.

turns.prompt_text: What are the ingredients I would need to take on this project?
turns.response_html:
Since you’re looking at doing this for a 2021 or 2022 Chevy Malibu, the "ingredients" for this project are pretty straightforward. Most hitches for this generation (like the CURT 11453 or Draw-Tite 24965) are designed as a bolt-on fit, meaning you won't have to do any drilling into the frame.

Here is the "shopping list" of everything you’ll need to have on your workbench before you start:

1. The Hardware (The "Ingredients")

  • The Hitch Receiver: Look for a Class 1 (1-1/4" receiver). These are specifically designed for the Malibu's unibody frame.
  • Vehicle-Specific Hardware Kit: (Usually included with the hitch)
    • Carriage Bolts & Square-Hole Spacers: These act as the mounting points inside your car’s frame.
    • Flange Nuts: To secure the hitch to those bolts.
    • Fish Wire (Pull Wire): This is a coiled wire tool used to "fish" the bolts through the frame holes. Don't lose this—it's the most important small part of the kit.

2. The Tool Kit

  • Torque Wrench: This is non-negotiable for safety. You’ll likely need to torque the bolts to around 50–75 lb-ft (check your specific hitch manual).
  • Sockets & Ratchet: Usually 11/16" and 3/4" (or 17mm and 19mm) deep-well sockets.
  • Exhaust Hanger Tool (or a Large Screwdriver): You’ll need to pry the rubber exhaust hangers off to drop the muffler slightly.
  • Soapy Water or Lubricant (WD-40): A quick spray on the rubber exhaust hangers makes them slide off (and back on) much easier.
  • Safety Gear: Since you'll be working directly under the chassis, safety glasses are a must to keep road grit out of your eyes.

A Note on the "Chef's Technique"

Because the Malibu’s frame is enclosed, you’ll be using a technique called Reverse Fish Wiring. You'll thread the bolt and spacer onto the wire, push them into the access hole, and then pull them back down through the same hole so the bolt hangs out for you to mount the hitch.
